name: zt-digest-base
description: The shared base of the ZT digest workflows. A digest builds only the book's Literature tree: Prepare, the book term table, the ledger-driven group cycle, the per-group Card checks, the whole-book card cycle, Link, Organize (the Literature index and the structure Card), Figures and the report-first Bridge between Literature trees, joined by the final audit, with slots where a book type installs its own layers (models, explanations, events, findings, math stages). Topic trees, Topic Cards, hubs and the concept register belong to zt-idea-grow.
whenToUse: Not run by itself: a variant (zt-econ-digest, zt-math-digest) names it in "base", sets consts.profile, and fills its slots

preflight.P1: Goal and result: the base is every stage that all ZT digests share (zt-digest-protocol sections 2-4), first ported from the hand-written zt-book-digest.js (removed 2026-10-16). The result is the report stage's object, in the shape that script returned for each mode, plus a variant's extra reports.
preflight.P2: Inputs: the args of the removed zt-book-digest.js, one declaration each (out required; citationKey, source, bibtex, bookTitle checked per mode by the args stage, as before). 2.4.0 adds book: a Scholar Archive Work id or exact title that resolves source, bibtex, bookTitle and the file through the read-only bridge, so mode full takes book or the three explicit arguments, never a silent mix. They carry data: paths, keys, pilot filters, batch sizes (capped at the DSMP limits in code), DeepSeek efforts (raised to high), and switches that pick among declared conditional stages. architectEffort is gone: the architect role's effort is frozen. Bridge arguments select limits (60/120 sources, 5/8 candidates), target books, report id and separate new/earlier acceptance; work is out/bridge. 3.0.0 adds maxAttempts (1-10, default 3) and dshRunCap (60-3600 s, default 1200): the only new run settings, persisted in the preparation contract by zt-digest prepare, so a resume reuses them. Leases, batch sizes and heartbeat intervals stay versioned tool defaults. 3.0.0 adds maxAttempts (1-10, default 3) and dshRunCap (60-3600 s, default 1200): the only new run settings, persisted in the preparation contract by zt-digest prepare, so a resume reuses them. Leases, batch sizes and heartbeat intervals stay versioned tool defaults.
preflight.P3: Units of work: the run ledger owns readiness. Digest groups are digest/gNNN@1 units claimed one block at a time; each group chain starts its own snapshot and job (R262) and records a checked completion with the owned-Card manifest its receipts prove. The Cards layer (cards/gNNN@1), the Model units (models/gNNN-mIIII@1), the explanations (explain/<key>@1), the Events and Findings units, the Terms unit (terms/book@1) and the whole-book card cycle (cards-book/book@N) are worked by a layer driver in bounded blocks. The concept review and the scoped restatement review are not separate units: their frozen files are work of the existing Terms and whole-book Card units, and their DeepSeek jobs are bounded chains of their own stages, so no concept or review table is added (D313, S23-AC02). Compiler jobs stay one Haiku manager per 8 jobs, at most 8 managers in the run (the global pool). 5.0.0: the concept review and the scoped restatement review left the base (they reviewed Topics and Topic Cards, which a digest no longer writes).
preflight.P4: Roles: manager = Haiku, effort low (relays commands, runs DeepSeek managers, clean-ups; reads no book, writes no Card). architect = Sonnet (writes plan.json only). organizer = Opus (writes decisions.json only). Scripts do every structural step; DeepSeek does the labour (DeepSeek Subagent Managed Protocol).
preflight.P5: Stage graph (readiness, R244): args → source → prepare → [after-prepare] → terms → digest (one ready group per manager chain) → cards (the per-group offline checks) → [after-digest: the model layer] → [after-models: explanations] → cards-book → link-prepare → link → link-check → [after-link] → organize (the Literature index and the structure Card) → figures → bridge (report-first, Literature trees only) → audit → finalize (the finite audit-plan → one correction cycle → publication refresh → final audit branch, R299/R300) → [after-audit] → cleanup → report. 5.0.0 (docs/literature-only-digest-design.md): a digest builds only the book's Literature tree. It creates no Topic tree, writes no Topic-tree Card, no Hub Card and no register, and links no Topic-tree Card; zt-idea-grow composes all of them from the Literature trees. The stages concepts, review, hubs-first and hubs and mode hubs are gone; every zt-digest step of the run writes in the Literature scope, which refuses such a write before it reaches the archive. The Event and Finding layers fill [after-terms] and are worked from ledger readiness while the remaining digest groups run; the model layer is released when the digest managers settle, and the whole-book card cycle waits for the Model reviews while model compilation never waits for it. A resume and every repair mode drain their downstream closure: mode resume runs terms, digest, Cards, every enabled layer, the whole-book cycle, link and link-check, Organize, Figures, Bridge, audit, finalize, the mathematics tail, cleanup and the report; modes models, explain, events and findings run their own layer, then the changed-Card Link pass and check, Organize, audit and the settlement (#87, R286).
preflight.P6: Modules (since 5.0.0; the history below names the removed ones): gate (args), zt-dsh-source, zt-digest-prepare, zt-book-terms, zt-group-cycle, zt-cards-layer, zt-cards-book, zt-link-prepare, zt-link-pass, zt-link-check, zt-organize, zt-figures, zt-dsh-cleanup, zt-audit, zt-finalize, zt-digest-report; all share zt-digest-lib v14. The book type installs its own prompt files and its layers in the slots. 3.5.0: a Link job owns only a group's own receipts, its anchor and its Literature-tree Cards, and a group whose digest unit is not done is reported blocked with an empty allow-list (#92); every claim requests a lease that covers dshRunCap, and a chain renews it after every wait on a running job (#92). 3.6.0: the Link pass computes each completed group's semantic gap set from its own receipts and schedules only the gaps; a gap-free group settles its Link unit with no provider run; the gap-stage prompt, the frozen job and the report carry the scheduled/skipped/gap counts and the L1/L2 quality (#110). 4.0.0: the delivered vertical paths join their existing stages (S23): zt-concepts drives `zt-digest concepts propose` (the run's own term rows are the proposed concepts) and the one judge job into the frozen review; zt-review drives `zt-digest restate` over the run's own staged owned-Card manifests and counts a recorded merge verdict only when a rewrite covers it; zt-hubs adds the `zt-digest register` plan after the hub publication and applies it only for the accepted plan id in `args.registerPlan`; the Bridge report runs before the hub and register plan, as §13.1 orders it. 4.0.1 (zt-digest-lib v14): the resource registration and observation commands create the resources folder with [System.IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory, because New-Item has no -LiteralPath and the old command recorded no run id. 4.0.2 (zt-digest-prepare v8): mode resume reads `ledger status -Summary` (the units counted per layer and state); the full status of a 171-group book, about 450 KB, was more than one relayed output line can carry. 4.1.0 (zt-digest-lib v15, zt-group-cycle v4, zt-link-pass v5, zt-dsh-cleanup v4): one Haiku manager runs a block of up to eight digest or Link units side by side (the protocol's eight DeepSeek conversations per manager), at most eight lanes; the digest stage is one module stage, no longer one manager chain per group. Every manager records its own DeepSeek ids and answers with plain `ledger resource -RegisterId/-EvidenceFor` commands, and the cleanup agents record their own facts with `-Settle/-SettleWorkspace`: no relay agent restates what another agent saw (a relay refused that as invented content), and no Haiku agent is spent per recorded fact. 4.1.1 (zt-digest-lib v16): a block manager that summarizes its claim line no longer stops its lane or strands a unit: the held units come from the manager's own unit reports when the claim line does not parse, a lane ends only on a claim that found no ready unit, and a JSON line with a trailing remark is still read. 4.2.0 (zt-digest-lib v17, zt-group-cycle v5, zt-link-pass v6): the ledger decides each block unit's outcome. After a block, one `ledger status -Units` reads the held units' states; a unit the ledger holds done is done whatever the manager reported, a unit another path settled is left alone, and only a unit the block still holds gets a fault (on stiglitz2014learning run 6, managers returned one of eight unit reports or none, and the module sent a `ledger fail` for each done unit, which the ledger refused). Block claims use `ledger next -Brief`, so the claim line carries no unit inputs. 4.3.0 (zt-digest-lib v19): every layer gate asks for `ledger gate -Brief` (the full status, about 49 KB, came back summarized), and a drive step's job list reaches its DeepSeek managers from the file the step command itself saved (`Tee-Object` → `<out>\jobs\<step>.json`): the module takes only the job ids from the relayed line, and each manager reads its jobs' exact files and prompts from that file (on grossman2002integration trial 2 a relay that retyped a long job list dropped part of a path and a derivation job failed). 4.4.0 (zt-digest-lib v20): a layer claim whose relayed line lost its units array reads the units it holds from the ledger by its owner label (`ledger status -Held "<label>"`) and works exactly those (on grossman2002integration trial 3 a relay retyped the cards claim's units as a sentence and the driver recorded a fault against an undefined unit). 4.5.0 (zt-digest-lib v21): every layer claim is brief (`ledger next -Brief` keeps of a unit's inputs only its Model address, `header`/`model`), a model or explain unit that arrives without its address is read from the ledger by owner, and a layer fault carries the claim's input hash (on trial 4 a relay dropped the inputs of four model units and the driver ran `model-finish -Model 'undefined'`; its fault was refused for an empty input hash). A layer gate is complete when its own layer is (`ledger gate -Brief`). 4.6.0 (zt-digest-lib v22): a layer finish whose relayed line is not readable JSON asks the ledger (`ledger status -Units <unit>`) before it records a fault, and a unit the ledger holds done stays done (on trial 5 a relay cut the end off a 2.5 KB cards completion and the driver tried to fault a done unit). The model and explain layer drivers hold every claim of a block with `ledger hold` (one bounded command after another, each renewing the claims every 60 s for up to 540 s and ending once none is held) while the work runs (zt-model-layer v3, zt-explain): on trial 5 four model claims expired while their models were still being built. 4.7.0 (zt-digest-lib v23, zt-model-lib v4, zt-dsh-cleanup v5): A layer's `rounds` bound only its consecutive claims that found nothing ready (at most 200 claims in all): on trial 6 the events and findings layers spent their three rounds on three productive claims while one digest group was still retrying, and stopped before that group's units appeared. The model chain runs `zt-digest model -Step close` after its last fill, derive or split and before its report: each build fault (closure, forward, reach-in, unanchored) goes back once, as a 修正 note, to the conversation that wrote the Card it sits in (on trial 6 model-finish refused all four models: a Model Card that 依赖 four Idea Cards of its group, and a 解读 sentence that 依赖 a later part), and the Model Card job tells its writer that an outside link never rests on. The cleanup stage records, before it settles anything, the evidence of every recorded conversation whose answer file a manager wrote but whose `-EvidenceFor` record never came (trial 6: two of three review jobs), so the verifier does not refuse them as `cleanup_evidence_missing`. 4.8.0 (zt-model-lib v5, zt-model-layer v4): each planned model registers its references to parts of models outside its batch with `zt-digest model-deps` after the plan and before the fill; a model whose producer is not done yet is released to wait (no model-finish now; the ledger readies it again), and a refused reference is recorded as that unit's content fault (on trial 8 batch 2 took `2|a#DA` from batch 1 and all three of its models failed at the fill). 4.8.0 also: the cleanup stage reads the brief resource listing (`ledger resource -List -Brief`: per workspace the recorded ids, the ones still open and the ones without evidence; zt-dsh-cleanup v6): the full listing, about 52 KB on trial 8, came back as prose and the cleanup settled nothing and rendered no run report. Organize, the skeleton, Figures and Bridge publish their own book revision at the end of their stage with `zt-digest finalize -Step stage -Layer <layer>` and their declared artifacts (zt-organize v3, zt-figures v3, zt-bridge v6): no stage published before, so `organize/book@1`, `skeleton/book@1`, `figures/book@1` and `bridge/book@1` stayed ready and no run could be content-complete. 4.9.0 (zt-model-lib v6): a model that `zt-digest model-deps` releases to wait, or whose reference it refuses, leaves its batch before the fill with `zt-digest model -Step defer -Models <list>` (out of the batch order, plan set aside as plan-deferred.json), and a batch left with no planned model fills nothing; a reference to a model the same batch planned is resolved by the compiler and makes nothing wait (on grossman2002integration trial 9 three of four models of the first batch were released to wait for `2|a`, built by the same batch, and the fill still held jobs for all four). The digest base prompt asks that every `$` of a formula be paired and that no text with `$` go through a PowerShell double-quoted string (zt-check R22 reports an open formula, hard, in the card cycle too), and files Literature-tree Cards by the argument: the next step of a Card is its Direct successor, and an anchor holds at most about 7 Side successors (on trial 8 every anchor held a flat fan of 6 to 12 Side successors and two titles lost `$A_I`). 4.9.1 (zt-digest-lib v24, zt-dsh-cleanup v7): every layer finish that is not plainly done asks the ledger (`ledger status -Units`) before it records a fault; on trial 10 a relay rewrote the end of a done cards completion as prose, the line still held a nested file record, and the driver faulted the done unit (the ledger refused it as stale). `model-deps` decides an in-batch reference by the plan.json in the batch folder, not by a plan hash the compiler records only at the fill (trial 10 still deferred `3|a`, `4|a` and `7|a` behind `2|a` of the same batch; the defer kept every write claimed). The model chain's close step also sends back every planned rests-on/of Link a written part does not author (model-finish refused trial 10's 7|a for 7|a|a|5 lacking its Link to 3|a|a|2 after close reported no fault). A card cycle whose plan line the relay rewrote is no failure when its report line reads (trial 10: the relay abridged the whole-book plan inside its jobs array, the cycle reported 0 faults after, and the stage faulted its claim as plan failed). zt-check counts a book title in 《…》 as one name and reads no prose rule on the Literature Card's document line, and the model compiler writes no semicolon into a 结构 line (trial 10's four residual hard faults: three R2 on the Literature and structure Cards, one R3 in 8|a's 共用 line). cleanup-finish accepts an explicit unavailable usage record and -EvidenceFor without -Usage writes one (trial 10: every digest cleanup unit refused as cleanup_evidence_missing), and the agent-facing resource record commands print one short line (a 260 KB -SettleWorkspace answer made the cleanup agent report six workspaces unrecorded). The cleanup claims its units until none is ready or every offered unit has failed three times in the stage (trial 10: three rounds of eight claims went to the same failing units and eight link cleanup units were never claimed). The digest base prompt files no Idea Card after a Model Card (trial 10 filed nine as Direct successors of 4|a and 8|a under the new chain rule). 4.9.2 (zt-dsh-cleanup v8): organize-apply rewrites the staging `owned-gNN.txt` and `src-gNN.txt` manifests through its moved map (grossman2002integration trial 11: a moved Topic Card kept its old address there and the notes cycle stopped at incomplete Card read; relocating the ledger outputs instead broke the checked fingerprints of the units already published on them). The cleanup stage passes no id list through a relay: it reads `ledger resource -List -Counts`, records missing evidence with `ledger resource -SweepEvidence`, and each deletion or workspace agent reads its own workspace's ids with `ledger resource -List -Workspace` (trial 11: the relay abridged the brief listing and left out the two model workspaces, so 83 conversations stayed and the run cleanup could not settle). The card cycle treats an Idea Card that I6 finds near a Model part as a fix target (D1: give it the part's missing angle and link the part, or merge); trial 11 had five such pairs. The agent-facing resource record commands name the recorded conversation or workspace and leave out the run id (a trial 11 brief manager read the run id as the registered one). zt-check reads no prose rule on a Model Card's 结构 list lines (compiler navigation), and the skeleton apply measures each index line with its group label (trial 11's two residual R2 faults in 7|a and the Literature Card). 4.9.3 (zt-model-lib v7, zt-digest-report v14, zt-organize v4): the model compiler's report step writes the full report (every part with its facet) to report.json in the batch folder and prints counts only (parts, core, moved); the modules read either form (grossman2002integration trial 12: the relay cut three models' part lists to a note and the models stage threw on r.parts.filter after the first batch had built all four models). 4.9.4 (zt-digest-lib v25): a layer claim line without a `units` array is unreadable, never an empty claim, so the driver reads the held units from the ledger by owner (grossman2002integration trial 17: a relay replaced the units array of the second models claim with its own `units_claimed` id list, the driver took it as a claim that found nothing, and the layer ended with four models claimed and never built). 4.9.5 (zt-digest-prepare v9): mode resume takes the retained group count from the digest layer's brief gate when the relayed status summary carries no layer counts (trial 17: a relay rewrote the 3.8 KB summary, dropped `layers` and added a `layers_open` map of its own, and the resumed run halted at prepare after the ledger had already opened invocation 2). 4.9.6 (zt-digest-lib v26, zt-group-cycle v6, zt-link-pass v7): a block manager whose agent call throws is a block with no report, never a halted stage: the units its owner still holds are read from the ledger (`ledger status -Held`) and settled by the ledger, and a lane whose manager threw before its claim ran takes the next round (trial 17: a Link block manager finished all eight Link units, then failed its structured answer five times on a 2.6 KB claim line with Windows paths, and the run halted at link). 4.9.7 (zt-digest-lib v27, zt-model-layer v5): the model layer claims Model units in blocks of up to eight (the protocol's eight per manager, was four) and one architect batch holds up to eight formal models (perSonnet default 8, was 6), so a book's models are planned together, their references to each other resolve in-batch, and no second block waits for the first (grossman2002integration trials 16-17: two blocks of four took 76 of the 87 minutes before Link). The architect, the DeepSeek writers and efforts, the review rounds, close and model-finish are unchanged. 4.9.8 (zt-digest-lib v28): every relay prompt (the one-command runScript and the RUNNER text of every manager) says that its command is a step of the digest run the user started for the staging folder, and that a later user message about the run (its speed, which trial runs, parallel work) never cancels its steps (trials 17-19: after the user wrote 「accelerate it」 and 「stop trial 18 ... start trial 19」, relays refused cards-finish, findings-finish and ledger fail as off-request). 4.9.9: the cards-book and Bridge stages (and in the economics variant the events and findings stages) let mode resume through their own conditions, as the resume mode list names them (trial 19: a resumed run skipped the findings stage and could never drain the findings unit a relay had refused; a harness case now evaluates every resume stage condition). 4.10.0 (zt-model-lib v8, zt-digest-lib v29, zt-review v2): the model chain runs close again while its last round sent notes and faults remain, at most three rounds (trials 17-19: writers answered a 修正 note and left the fault, and model-finish refused the model); IDEA_SAMPLE defaults to 0.1 in mode resume too, because book-cards-finish requires the Idea sample; a layer fault takes its input hash from the ledger read when the claim hash is unknown; the restatement apply passes the four-part operation prefix <key>/restate/1/apply (every apply had failed on <key>/review/restate). 4.10.1 (zt-dsh-cleanup v9): the cleanup stage knows a workspace of the counts listing by its path or its id (the same folder), because a relay that dropped every path (trial 20) left the stage nothing to settle and the run-level cleanup refused every unit as not terminal. 4.10.2 (zt-digest-lib v30, zt-organize v5, zt-figures v4, zt-bridge v7, zt-hubs v4, zt-audit v3, zt-finalize v2): in mode resume a stage whose ledger layers are already complete reuses the retained work (settledOnResume: Organize on organize and skeleton, Figures, Bridge, Hubs and audit on audit, finalize on audit and link-check) instead of redoing it (trial 20: the resume reran Organize, which can merge or move finished Cards). 4.11.0 (zt-digest-lib v31, zt-digest-prepare v10; Tree Lock S17, #140): a write the owner's Lock refused is a planning error, not a provider fault. The library reads the archive's typed `card_locked` JSON out of a failed step, a claimed unit's start or checked finish, or a refused chain step, keeps it as that unit's content fault and stops the affected stage with the refusal (R326/R337/R338): the drafts, errors and receipts already written stay, and nothing is retried, unlocked or re-pointed through another write path. Preparation stops with the same refusal before its first write. 5.0.0 (zt-organize v6, zt-digest-report v15, zt-digest-prepare v11): the digest builds only the Literature tree. zt-concepts, zt-review and zt-hubs leave the base (the hub, register and Topic work is zt-idea-grow's); Organize decides the thesis and the notes on the book's own Cards only (no Topic merge, no move, no Topic body, no legacy Opus job); the report has no concept, review, hub or register entries; the prepared run freezes no hubs switch (the ledger excludes the hubs layer and refuses run option hubs). The prompts file every Card in the Literature tree, and zt-digest refuses create_topic, a Topic-tree or Hub write and a Link to a Topic-tree Card in every digest step (the Literature scope). 5.1.0 (zt-digest-lib v33, zt-digest-report v16): the whole report carries next, the zt-idea-grow run (this book, a fresh out folder) that grows the book's Topic Cards, hubs and register, and the report stage logs it; the library loses the hub settings and the hub compiler's self-check in its approval rules, and the unreachable modules zt-concepts, zt-review and zt-hubs are deleted; the Card, Event, Finding and orphan prompts give Literature-tree addresses in their examples. 5.1.1 (zt-link-check v2): the Link check stage publishes its own link-check revision from its cycle report with `zt-digest finalize -Step stage -Layer link-check` (zt-digest 0.11.3 accepts it); the finalization refreshes that revision only when its one correction cycle changed a Card, so on acemoglu2025nobel trial 1, whose final audit found nothing to correct, link-check/book@1 stayed ready and the run was never content-complete. zt-digest 0.11.3 also creates the link-jobs folder in link-start (trial 1: every Link job failed to start in a folder nothing had created), names the jobs already applied in the event and finding plan line (applied_jobs), and gives the model close line a status (clean, follow_up or unresolved). 5.1.2 (zt-digest-lib v34, zt-dsh-cleanup v10; zt-digest 0.11.4), from ebrill2001modern trial 1: a claim command that fails is tried again, three times in all, before its layer hears of it (one `ledger next` refused while parallel lanes changed the archive, and the events layer ended with 40 of 73 units unclaimed). The cleanup stage settles its units with one command, `zt-digest cleanup-finish -Ready`, which claims every ready cleanup unit, runs each checked verifier (the run-level unit last), and records a retryable fault with the claim's own hash for a unit that cannot settle yet (the stage had spent one Haiku agent per unit, about 150 one after another, and sent its faults with an empty input hash, which `ledger fail` refused, so the failed units stayed claimed; `ledger fail` now takes the claim's hash when a fault names none). A workspace the provider no longer knows is recorded removed (the resume recorded the workspaces trial 1 had removed as not removed, and cleanup/book@1 could not settle). The plain record commands -Settle, -SettleWorkspace and -EvidenceFor take the claim holder's -Unit and -Token, and a claim whose lease ran out no longer fences them. -RegisterId refuses a placeholder such as PENDING (an explain manager had registered one to try the command), and every manager prompt says to register only the session_id deepseek_run returned and to start no run for a step with no job (a findings manager sent the prompt "placeholder" to DeepSeek and left a stray conversation).
preflight.P7: Checks: every DeepSeek job runs its SELF-CHECK (in the job files the scripts write); zt-check is the only checker; the args stage checks the required args per mode and the kernel validates the finite bounds of maxAttempts and dshRunCap; the group finish applies and checks the persisted digest outputs; each layer records its checked completion evidence and its gate; the report keeps each stage's status, the effective settings and the schedule summary. BR1–BR9 and Card checks gate reports and accepted edits.
preflight.P8: Failure policy (R259): args, source, prepare, digest (no ready unit could be verified) and link-prepare halt. terms, organize, bridge, finalize and cleanup continue on a failure: a residual hard fault is finalize's partial result, never a halted run. A layer records a content failure against its own unit (`ledger fail -Class content`) and keeps the stage going; a transient transport, lease or provider fault is retryable and that unit is claimed again within maxAttempts, never by rerunning the stage (R258). Modes: link, cards, figures, audit and bridge; a book type adds its own (models, explain, events, findings, math, resume). Checkpoint: digest (stop before the Cards layer and the book type stages). Mode resume accepts only out: it reads the retained identity, source choices, Citation key, enabled layers, versions and existing authorization-bound selections from the ledger, runs the one supported `ledger resume` (invocation 2, resume_count, only the unresolved units reset, blocked dependants back to dependency evaluation) and never a second resume (#87, R274-R285). A group whose digest unit is not done gets no link job: the link preparation reports it blocked with an empty allow-list and the report names it (#92). A group with no semantic gap starts no provider run: its Link unit settles from the empty checked draft and the report counts it as skipped (#110). A write that the Literature scope refuses (`literature_only`: create_topic, a Topic-tree or Hub Card, a Link to a Topic-tree Card) is the writer's content fault: the draft or job is corrected, never written through another path. A destination tree the owner locked answers the typed `card_locked` refusal (R326): the affected write stage stops with that refusal and the stages after it do not run, the atomic batch it asked for wrote nothing, and the receipts committed earlier are not undone (R337). No stage reads the refusal as a provider fault or retries it.
preflight.P9: Dry run: zt-econ-digest.sim.json and zt-math-digest.sim.json take mode full through every stage. Fixture: tests/framework-harness.mjs checks the readiness graph (terms before the group writers, the whole-book cycle before the gap-only Link pass, Bridge after Figures and before the audit, no concept, review or hub stage, and the finite finalization last), the joins, the group cycle and layer commands, the runner restrictions, the settings on the built scripts, the delivered paths (no gaps, a failed group, a resumed prepared run) and the four finalization branches. Pilot: one chapter with cardMax and explainMax, after a database backup. 5.0.1 (base 5.0.1, zt-digest-lib v32): every approval rule that lets a DeepSeek job run the zt helper refuses a helper command with -Open, which would leave the Literature scope; no stage, data-flow, param or role change. 5.1.0: the harness checks the next line of the whole report and that no approval rule offers the hub compiler.

manager.description: Haiku: relays one script command, runs DeepSeek managers and clean-ups

architect.description: Sonnet: the model architect, writes plan.json only

organizer.description: Opus: the Organize decisions, writes decisions.json only

citationKey.description: the book's BibTeX key (all modes but audit)

source.description: the book's Chinese or bilingual Markdown (mode full)

book.description: a Scholar Archive Work id or an exact title: mode full resolves the Work, its Chinese/bilingual Markdown, the BibTeX and the heading range instead of source, bibtex and bookTitle

fileId.description: the book Markdown's Scholar Archive file id

startHeading.description: the Chinese heading where the digested text starts

endHeading.description: the Chinese heading where the digested text stops

skipHeadings.description: headings whose units are left out, e.g. 参考文献,习题

groups.description: the existing group count (modes link and models)

organize.description: true: Organize after modes link and models (the Literature index, the structure Card and the notes on the book's own Cards)

perManager.description: digest groups per Haiku manager (default 5, at most 8)

maxChars.description: the most characters of a group (default 20000)

maxUnits.description: the most units of a group (default 3)

dshSource.description: where DeepSeek V4.1 Flash runs; auto probes official, then OpenCode Go

dshModel.description: a DeepSeek Harness model that overrides dshSource

dshEffort.description: DeepSeek effort of digest, link, and fill runs (raised to high)

rebuild.description: rebuild models that already have parts

dshPerBatch.description: DeepSeek runs one Haiku manager keeps going (default 8, at most 8)

dshManagers.description: Haiku managers of one compiler step in parallel (default 8, at most 8)

linkPerManager.description: link runs one Haiku manager starts at once (default 8)

applyShare.description: jobs one card-cycle apply call writes (default 30)

only.description: the Model Card addresses to work on (a pilot)

level.description: build every model of the run to this level

briefEffort.description: DeepSeek effort of the briefs (raised to high)

deriveEffort.description: DeepSeek effort of the Derivation parts (raised to high)

reviewEffort.description: DeepSeek effort of the review (raised to high)

maxSentences.description: Card size of a formal model part: sentences (default 12)

maxPartChars.description: Card size of a formal model part: characters (default 400)

terms.description: mode full: false skips the book term table

audit.description: mode full: false skips the audit

finalize.description: mode full: false skips the finite finalization branch (audit plan, one scoped correction cycle, publication refresh, final read-only audit)

figures.description: mode full: false skips the Figures stage

cardChecks.description: modes full and link: false skips the card layer cycle

ideaSample.description: share of fault-free Idea Cards reviewed against the source (mode full: 0.1)

cardRules.description: the rules the card cycle fixes (default all hard rules)

cardMax.description: a pilot: at most this many Cards with faults and orphans

explainMax.description: mode explain, a pilot: at most this many Derivation parts

bridge.description: full mode: false skips Bridge discovery

bridgeCandidates.description: similarity candidates per source, default 5 plus at most two literal matches

bridgeReport.description: exact published report id; only mode bridge

bridgeApply.description: all or a unique array of new-carrier ids from bridgeReport

bridgeApplyEarlier.description: separate all or unique array of earlier-carrier ids from bridgeReport

maxAttempts.description: the per-unit attempt budget of the managed run (default 3); persisted at preparation

dshRunCap.description: the seconds one external DeepSeek run may live (default 1200); persisted at preparation

checks.message: args must be an object with citationKey
mode full needs args book, or args source, bibtex, and bookTitle
Bridge acceptance requires mode bridge, a report id, and a nonempty selection
bridgeMax must be a whole number in 1..120
bridgeCandidates must be a whole number in 1..8

mode resume reads the retained identity, source, Citation key, enabled layers and settings from its ledger and accepts only out: a new identity, source, group count, model list or Bridge selection needs its own preparation

stages.title: Prepare
stages.detail: the DeepSeek source (probe official, then OpenCode Go)

stages.title: Prepare
stages.detail: Chinese-only book text, section groups, the Literature tree with anchors, the shared prefixes

stages.title: Prepare
stages.detail: the book term table (book-terms.ps1 and one DeepSeek job)

stages.title: Digest
stages.detail: the group cycle in blocks: one manager claims up to 8 digest/gNNN@1 units, a snapshot and frozen job per group, their DeepSeek runs side by side, each conversation recorded and deleted by that manager, checked group-finish (R250/R252/R253); at most 8 lanes

stages.title: Cards
stages.detail: the per-group offline Card checks (cards/gNNN@1), claimed from the ready work and recorded by cards-finish

stages.title: Cards
stages.detail: one whole-book card cycle after the digest runs (mode full), or on its own (mode cards); it also reviews the source of every Model draft no model chain elaborates

stages.title: Link
stages.detail: prepare-link-pass.ps1: the receipt-owned semantic gap set and the scheduled, gap-free and blocked groups

stages.title: Link
stages.detail: DeepSeek Link runs fill only the receipt-owned semantic gaps

stages.title: Cards
stages.detail: the card layer cycle on the new Links and the orphans

stages.title: Organize
stages.detail: survey → Opus thesis and notes (decisions.json) → apply (no merge, no move) → notes card cycle → skeleton (the Literature index and the structure Card)

stages.title: Figures
stages.detail: attach-figures.ps1: the book's own figures in the Cards that name them

stages.title: Bridge
stages.detail: bounded frozen cross-book discovery and immutable review report; explicit accepted apply in bridge mode

stages.title: Audit
stages.detail: digest-audit.ps1, read-only: faults per rule, orphans, models, figures (it counts the box's Topic trees and hubs as information, never as a digest fault)

stages.title: Finalize
stages.detail: the finite finalization: the audit plan, at most one compiler correction cycle scoped to its Cards, the changed-Card/touched-tree manifest, the dependency-scoped publication refresh, and the final read-only audit

stages.title: Cleanup
stages.detail: settle every DeepSeek conversation and workspace the run recorded, delete exactly those ids, remove only registered scratch inside the staging root, then render the verified run report (completeness, gaps, current placeholders, timings, exact per-run usage), reporting content_complete apart from cleanup_complete
